handoff: Review approve: AC1-AC7 (B3, B5-B10, B12) each traced to a test that asserts it; unit tier 1130/0, typecheck green, version-guard integration 11/0. No blocking findings; minor: a broken config lets config set run on a mismatch (on purpose), and the no-key AC7 test is thin; two nits.

findings.title: A broken config lets acts commands that never load config run on a mismatch
findings.detail:
guardVersion returns when !loaded.ok, so the guard trusts the command to raise the config error itself. config set/unset (config-edit.ts) never reads ctx.config, so with any config problem plus a mismatched binary it writes a config file. B6 says a wrong binary never writes state; a config file is not unit state, and the handoff says this is on purpose (a broken file must stay fixable), so it is minor.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Keep it, and note in the spec's D2 that config edits get through when the config is broken; or, when !loaded.ok, check the version from the team file alone if it parses.

findings.title: The 'no key, every command runs as before' test runs three commands
findings.detail:
AC7 says no key means every command runs as before; the test runs tick, config set and brief. The guard's early return on a null key covers the rest, and the rest of the integration tier runs without the key, so the coverage holds in practice.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optional: run the AC2 argv table with the key absent and assert no version_mismatch code.

findings.title: comparable() regex is not anchored at the end
findings.detail:
/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+/ also takes '0.19.0.1' or '0.19.0abc' as 0.19.0. Harmless for real versions.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Anchor on (?=$|[-+]).

findings.title: Trailing blank line at the end of the file
findings.detail:
The file ends with an extra empty line.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Remove it.
